title: Exploring Generalizable Automated Program Repair with Large Language Models
task: Empirical evaluation of LLM-based automated program repair, pass@1/pass@5 plausible patch generation across languages, prompt ingredients, fault localization granularity and patch complexity.
input_setting: Buggy single-function code; zero-shot prompt with optional failing test/error data, perfect function/line localization, or top-3 FLACOCO suspect functions on Defects4J; generate 15 patches/task across three runs.
author_relationship_evidence: Paper §7 Data Availability links exact Figshare share item; item title names the study and page metadata refers to its published IEEE Access version. The item indicates results/generated-patch supplement. No author code repository linked or located.
source_commit_or_archive: Figshare shared supplemental item (457.69 MB, modified 2026-07-14); no public repository commit identified.
license: Figshare metadata states CC BY 4.0 for supplement. No implementation code/license identified.
exact_models: 13 models: GPT-4o (dated version 2024-11-11), OpenAI o3-mini (2025-01-31), Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Claude 3.5 Haiku, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Gemini 2.0 Flash, CodeLlama 13B/70B, Llama 3.3 70B, DeepSeek Coder 33B, DeepSeek R1 distill 70B, Qwen 2.5 Coder 32B, CodeGemma 7B.
15 patch generations/task, three batches of five, temperature 1.0.
weights_status: No fine-tuning. Proprietary model endpoints needed for closed-model results; open-weight model names given but exact immutable weights/revisions are not pinned in available paper text.
evaluation_route: Paper reports pass@1/pass@5 on four real bug datasets, prompt/FL/complexity variants; result/generated-patch supplement is linked through a Figshare private-share page (457.69 MB, CC BY 4.0), but file downloads were not available in this anonymous check. No source/scripts repository located. No code execution, patch generation, or API call performed.
blockers: This is an APR evaluation, not reproduction-test generation or bug-root-cause taxonomy; it does not itself give human causal labels for bugs.

No author implementation or runnable experiment scripts were found. Figshare contains a large supplement but labels the item shared privately; web download returned 403 and anonymous HTTP HEAD returned 202 without content. The paper’s v2 says a reproduction package with prompting/analysis scripts would be added after acceptance, but accessible page does not document or expose those scripts.

Four dataset cohort counts are not reconciled between prose and Table 1: Defects4J 854 vs 845; BugsJS 453 vs 513; BugsPHP test split 513 vs Table 1 452; BugsInPy single-hunk 82 reproducible used vs 132 in Table 1. These may reflect filtering/version but method does not explain the differences in the read text.

The study generated ~195k patches across 13 models and four languages; closed models require API access and exact provider revisions are not pinned for all model families. Full rerun is expensive and the paper gives no total budget.
Evaluation relies on plausible-patch test pass rate, not manual patch correctness; authors discuss overfitting and contamination risks.
concept_fit: Low-to-moderate for the test-generation thesis: useful evidence that test diagnostics and realistic imperfect localization affect repair, and that cross-language bug datasets have reproducibility issues. It does not generate tests or identify underlying bug causes.
recommendation: Use as supporting background for choosing Defects4J/BugsInPy cohorts and designing imperfect-localization controls, not as the main thesis paper. The analysis suggests test failure signals help repair but does not answer root-cause taxonomy. Reproduction is conditional on obtaining the private-share supplement/scripts, resolving dataset denominators, and allocating multi-model API/compute budget.
